s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to antibiotics, suggesting an immune-related process
salient_findings: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
key_facts: 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma
Treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
Follow-up chest CT showed new bilateral infiltrative shadows
Reported fever and dyspnea
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative
Serologic testing for various antibodies was negative
No history of antigen exposure
Immunotherapy was discontinued
Received lascufloxacin and tazobactam/ceftolozane without improvement
Oxygen requirement increased to 2 L/min
Chest radiographs remained unchanged after methylprednisolone and prednisolone treatment
Oxygen needs rose to 4 L/min
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages, and a CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy

shortlist.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab, and developed bilateral infiltrative shadows and symptoms consistent with pneumonitis

shortlist.label: Organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to antibiotics, which could be consistent with organizing pneumonia

shortlist.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although ruled out due to lack of antigen exposure, it remains a possible differential due to the patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and imaging findings could be consistent with cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, although the exact cause is unknown

shortlist.label: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and imaging findings could be consistent with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia, which is a possible differential given the patient's lack of response to antibiotics and immunotherapy

raw.rationale: The patient was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab, and after eight courses, he developed new bilateral infiltrative shadows, fever, and dyspnea, which are consistent with immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis. The negative serologic testing, lack of antigen exposure, and failure to respond to antibiotics also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic clinical and radiographic features

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: Transbronchial lung biopsy did not show characteristic features

rejected.label: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
rejected.why: Clinical and radiographic features are more consistent with immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
